messages:
maria.k: FYI we have a customer onboarding for an on‑prem/private deployment next week. They want strong isolation + KMS integration. Quick checklist request: default egress policy, operator RBAC, audit log shipping, and key rotation cadence. any hot takes?
kevin.l: Default-deny egress at the cluster/network layer is the easiest win. Cilium/Calico networkpols + an egress proxy for allowed destinations. Keep control-plane outbound minimal (NTP, CRL/OCSP, KMS endpoint).
ashley: Agree. For on‑prem we usually recommend: 1) default deny all egress 2) explicit egress proxy for telemetry/updates 3) break out jumpbox for operator access. Also put NAT on a restricted subnet if they need internet.
jin: RBAC: don't give platform team cluster-admin. Create a scoped "customer-ops" role bound to namespaces + custom verbs for node/drain only when approved. Use ephemeral creds (SPIRE or step-ca) for human/operator sessions. Record every sudo/exec in audit logs.
maria.k: For KMS: they want HSM-backed keys and customer-controlled rotation. How do we wire disk encryption + model artifact wrap keys so we can rotate without re-encrypting everything?
ashley: Use envelope encryption: data keys encrypted with CMK (customer-managed HSM key). Store encrypted data key alongside object metadata. Rotation = rewrap encrypted data keys with new CMK; no re-encrypt of payloads. We run a small rewrap job for a namespace when they request full rewrap.
ashley: Example (pseudo):
```bash
# generate DEK, wrap with CMK
DEK=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
WRAPPED=$(kms-cli wrap --key customer/keys/model-cmk --plaintext $DEK)
# store WRAPPED in object metadata, use DEK for encryption locally
```
kevin.l: Also need to ensure KMS endpoint connectivity is allowed from the private network, preferably via a customer-managed proxy or VPC peering. No direct public egress unless strictly audited.
pablo: From vuln triage: note the latest kernel CVE we flagged requires we disallow untrusted container runtimes on customer nodes. Add runtimeClass whitelist and image signature verification (cosign).
jin: Good call. Policy list: PodSecurity (runtimeClass), image signing, network default-deny, hostPath disallow, seccomp + AppArmor profiles.
maria.k: Audit logging: customer wants logs shipped to their SIEM AND retained for 1y. We currently have fluentd/otel options and an agent that can push to syslog/HTTP. Any pitfalls?
audit-bot: audit:collection: rule added -> cluster-audit -> forward to syslog-forwarder. See https://internal.ops/redwood/audit for config.
ashley: Pitfall: audit volume + PII. Need field-level scrubbing or a side-channel to send raw logs only to customer. Also ensure immutable storage for tamper evidence (WORM or object locking).
jin: Incident response quick play: 1) isolate affected nodes (cordon + drain to isolated pool), 2) revoke/rotate CMKs and ephemeral certs, 3) snapshot audit logs and push to secure bucket, 4) run forensics image of host, 5) update ACLs to block suspected egress. Documented TTLs for keys must match legal requirements.
pablo: Add a canary alert for unexpected KMS API usage patterns (high rewraps or new principals). Those are early indicators of key misuse.
maria.k: Awesome — I'll assemble a one-page checklist for the customer and a runbook for us. Can someone paste a NetworkPolicy example for default deny + egress to kms + metrics? e.g.
kevin.l: Yup, quick Cilium/NetworkPolicy example: 
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: default-deny-egress
  namespace: redwood-customer
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.10.0.0/24 # internal proxy/nat
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 192.0.2.0/28 # KMS proxy
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```
kevin.l: Tailor IPs to their network. Also log dropped packets at the egress proxy for forensics.
maria.k: Thanks team. I'll upload the checklist + runbook draft later today and tag you for review. :thumbsup:
kevin.l: lgtm, ping me on the runbook for the RBAC snippets.
jin: I'll add the SPIRE/ephemeral cert steps.
audit-bot: rule:runbook-review created -> #sec-runbook-reviews.
